title: All-Purpose Biscuits
summary: Tall, flaky biscuits from a food processor, folded three times and rested before cutting.

steps.title: Dry ingredients
steps.text: Sift the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt into a large bowl, then move it to a food processor.

steps.title: Cut in the butter
steps.text: Add the butter and pulse 5 or 6 times, just until it looks like rough crumbs. A fork or pastry cutter in the bowl works too.

steps.title: Add the milk
steps.text: Return it to the bowl, add the milk, and stir with a fork until it comes together in a rough ball.

steps.title: Fold three times
steps.text: On a well-floured counter, pat the dough into a rough rectangle about an inch thick. Fold it over and pat it down again. Do this three times total. The folds make the flaky layers.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover loosely with a towel and let it rest.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Pat it out to about 10 by 6 inches and cut with a floured cutter. Press straight down without twisting; twisting seals the edges and the biscuits won't rise as tall.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake on a sheet pan until golden brown.

notes: Makes 6 to 8. Double it for the family; it takes no extra time. Also good with sausage gravy, ham, or honey.
